name: _convert_indices_from_coo_to_csr
description: Representative ATen signature, copied verbatim from the supplied schema and not an exclusive ABI: aten::_convert_indices_from_coo_to_csr(Tensor self, int size, *, bool out_int32=False) -> Tensor. The other registered schema of the same ATen operator family is: aten::_convert_indices_from_coo_to_csr.out(Tensor self, int size, *, bool out_int32=False, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and its coverage must not be narrowed or removed to fit this one signature. Both registered schemas listed above are reproduced verbatim from the supplied schema evidence. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator consumes a rank-0 or rank-1 sorted COO row-index vector of integral dtype (int8/uint8/int16/int32, plus int64 where the device publishes int64 input support) plus an int row count `size`, and returns the CSR row-pointer tensor of length size + 1 with out[0] == 0 and out[r + 1] == out[r] + count(r). With out_int32 omitted the pointer tensor is int64 by default; out_int32=True produces int32 pointers. size must be a non-negative int: an empty index vector is valid for size >= 0, size == 0 returns the single pointer [0], and a non-empty vector needs size >= 1. Negative, float, None and string sizes, rank >= 2 index tensors, and unsupported input dtypes are rejected; the supplied negative tests assert these exceptions on the candidate only, and the unsupported-dtype and NaN/Inf rows are collected only on the measured NVIDIA build and only for dtypes the device can represent, so that rejection is asserted for that measured build and is not claimed for other vendors or builds. Only the string value "x" is probed as a wrong-typed out_int32. Sortedness is not validated natively. A unit-stride view with a non-zero storage offset is honoured, while strided views are not asserted. The .out overload writes into the caller-supplied buffer and returns that same buffer object; that aliasing and mutation behaviour is conditional on the overload and is defined by the original pytest, so this definition describes only the representative default overload's return.
